title: Can two sides and an angle ever fail to make a triangle?
description: The video tries a base of three centimetres, an arm of seven centimetres and different angles, and watches when the free ends can be joined. The angle is tried at one hundred and eighty degrees, at zero degrees, past one hundred and eighty, and between zero and one hundred and eighty.
teaching_notes: One idea: the arm must leave the base, and a protractor angle of a triangle is less than a straight angle. Watch for children who say a triangle always exists once two sides and an angle are given.

source: We have seen that triangles do not exist for all sets of sidelengths. Is there a combination of measurements in the case of two sides and the included angle where a triangle is not possible? Justify your answer using what you observe during construction.
video_script.why: The child can draw a triangle from two sides and the angle between them and now asks whether every such set works.
video_script.substitution: Draw a base, make an angle at one end, mark the second side along the arm and try to join, for angles of different sizes.
video_script.anchor: two sides and the angle between them, with a question mark: is there a set that gives no triangle
video_script.payoff_line: No triangle forms when the angle is one hundred and eighty degrees or more, or zero

final_answer.spoken: yes, no triangle forms when the angle is one hundred and eighty degrees or more, or zero

maths_rules: with the angle 180° the arm points straight out along the base line, so A, B and C lie on one straight line and there is no triangle
with the angle 0° the arm lies on top of the base, so A, B and C again lie on one line and there is no triangle
an angle of 180° or more, for example 210°, cannot be the angle of a triangle, since the angle of a triangle is less than a straight angle
for any angle strictly between 0° and 180° the arm leaves the base, C is off the base line, and joining B and C gives a triangle
video_script.design: One base and one arm are redrawn for each angle tried: 180 degrees, 0 degrees, past 180 degrees, and an angle in between. The ruler line along the base shows whether C lies on it.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes. No triangle forms when the angle is one hundred and eighty degrees or more, or zero.
